verdicts.reason: Photo shows the number '42' stenciled in yellow on a dark surface, evoking the forties but not showing the subject of the reading (a person in their forties, reflection, or turning point).

Photo shows a lit candle, a written list/paper, and a botanical sprig on a wooden surface — exactly the ritual props described in the tutorial (three candles, a written list of what you are bringing forward).
Photo shows a candle, a small bowl, dried botanical stems, and a piece of paper with 'Ancestor.' written on it — a flux-schnell generated image that precisely depicts this ritual's materials.
Photo shows properly browned pork sausages in a dark frying pan — the sausage element of bangers and mash is clear, but mash and onion gravy are absent so it is not the complete finished dish.

Photo shows a dark-sauced braised beef stew with carrots and mushrooms over mash in a floral bowl, which is the right class of dish but could be any beef braise rather than specifically Beef and Guinness Stew.
Photo shows sliced beef steak with foie gras and salad garnish on a fine-dining plate — not beef stew with herb dumplings in a pot.
Photo shows a large piece of golden battered fish with chips and curry sauce on a dark plate — a clear beer-battered fish supper, matching the finished dish.
Photo shows a circular braided rag rug (clearly braided and coiled fabric strips) — right craft and technique but the shape is round rather than the oval specified in the tutorial title.
Photo shows skeins of undyed natural white yarn in a bowl beside dyeing equipment — the wool ready for dyeing is present but no bundle-wrapping with plant material or dyed output is shown.

Photo shows a vintage typewriter with a sheet of paper reading 'CANCEL' — directly and unambiguously illustrates the act of cancelling a commitment, which is the exact subject of this activity tutorial.
Photo shows sliced pears on a cutting board with a jar of honey and a honey dipper — shows the pear wood source and honey context but not the carved honey stirrer itself.
Photo shows scissors, pliers, a knife, and a hammer displayed against a wooden carved chair — general repair tools, with no fallen branches or green-wood carving content.
Photo shows three spiral flaky pastries (pain aux raisins / Danish-style swirls) — not a shortcrust crimped cheese and onion pasty.
Photo shows a closed grilled cheese panini sandwich with grill marks on a white plate — contains cheese and bread but is a pressed sandwich rather than open-face toast with grill-bubbled cheddar.
Photo shows roasted/grilled chicken breast pieces with peas on a dark plate — not a chicken and ham pie under puff pastry.
Photo shows chicken pieces being pan-fried in a shallow pan — shows the right main ingredient being cooked but not the finished chicken and leek pie under puff pastry.
Photo shows an Asian-style stir-fry of chicken and mushrooms in a white bowl with spring onions — not a British chicken and mushroom pie under golden puff pastry.
Photo shows a person's stained hands lifting indigo-dyed fabric from a large deep-blue indigo vat — exactly depicts the cold-water indigo vat process.

Photo shows a plate with what appears to be fried meat patties with fried eggs on top, garnished with vegetables — has some hash-like elements (fried meat, eggs) but presented in a tortilla/flatbread style more reminiscent of Mexican food than British corned beef hash.
Photo shows sliced grilled beef steak on a wooden board with tomatoes and a steak knife — no pastry, no crimped edge, nothing resembling a Cornish pasty.
Photo shows marinated chicken pieces grilling on a BBQ rack — not cold poached chicken folded into curried mayonnaise dressing.
Photo shows raw beef mince in a glass bowl — shows the key ingredient but not the finished cottage pie with mash crust baked until golden.
Photo shows a tray of halved hard-boiled eggs with piped bright-yellow yolk filling and chive garnish — unambiguously devilled eggs.

Photo shows sliced dark meat in a rich brown sauce over white mash with vegetable garnish — has the right appearance of offal in a savoury sauce but is too ambiguous to confirm it is specifically lamb kidneys in Worcestershire-mustard sauce.
Photo shows whole raw fish being cut on a stone surface at what appears to be a fish market — shows fish (possibly mackerel family) being prepared but not devilled fillets grilled until charred.
Photo shows a feathery golden-green plant in close-up that resembles goldenrod or a similar Solidago-type plant — shows the dye plant but not the dyeing process or the dyed yarn output.
Photo shows an arrangement of yellow/orange marigold (Tagetes) flowers with red roses — the named dye botanical (marigold petals) is clearly and unambiguously the photograph's subject.

Photo shows blue-dyed fabric with a shibori/tie-dye resist pattern in indigo blue — shows woad/indigo-dyed cloth which is the right output colour and fibre but not the woad leaf extraction vat process itself.
Photo shows skeins of undyed natural white yarn in a bowl — the subject is walnut-hull dyeing which produces brown-dyed wool, and this image shows the opposite: undyed white yarn.
Photo shows stacks of brightly coloured woven textiles (Mexican-style striped blankets/rugs) — woven cloth is the right class but these are not handwoven cloth being wet-finished off a loom.
Photo shows a round salmon and herb frittata/omelette with a slice cut out — not a fish pie with smoked haddock, salmon, and prawns under a mashed-potato crust.
Photo shows a person holding a restaurant guest-check receipt — a bill from a diner, not a body-scan meditation connecting head and gut awareness.

Photo shows a pile of colourful needle-felted wool balls — these are felted wool objects which confirms the felting category, but they are 3D balls not flat felt sheets which is the tutorial's specific subject.
Photo shows Scrabble letter tiles spelling 'FORGIVE' with dried flowers in the background — the word forgiveness is the direct named subject of this affirmation tutorial.

Photo shows a dark herringbone-twill woven jacket/coat folded on a grey surface with a hat — the herringbone fabric pattern matches the tutorial's output but shows a finished garment rather than the weaving process or loom cloth.
Photo shows an extreme close-up of dusky-rose woven fabric with a clear raised hexagonal/honeycomb cell pattern — exactly the characteristic surface texture produced by honeycomb weave.

Photo shows two women hand-processing large amounts of raw fleece/wool outdoors — shows the right class of activity (hand-working raw fleece) but not the specific tool (hand cards) or output (rolags).
Photo shows a person seated with both hands resting gently on their belly/abdomen area — precisely depicts the named physical gesture (hand on belly) that is the tutorial's subject.

Photo shows a geometric-patterned rug on a floor with a trainer/sneaker in frame — the geometric pattern is correct but this appears to be a commercial flatwoven rug rather than a wool-hooked rug being worked.
Photo shows a light-box sign reading 'MAKE YOURSELF AT HOME' — connects to the home theme of the tutorial but is a motivational sign rather than imagery of home habits or domestic life.
Photo shows a rusted industrial metal surface stenciled with 'SAFETY FIRST' — an industrial safety reference with no connection to a body-scan meditation for inner calm.

Photo shows a bowl of clear-broth stew with chunks of lamb, potato, and carrot on a checked cloth alongside crusty bread — exactly matches Irish stew's defining characteristics (clear broth, lamb, potato, carrot).
Photo shows white fish pieces in a creamy white sauce in a shallow bowl — not kedgeree, which should be spiced buttered rice with flaked smoked haddock and hard-boiled eggs.
Photo shows two live young lambs lying in a green field — not the finished Lancashire hotpot dish with its characteristic overlapping-potato golden crust.
Photo shows a lit pillar candle with an envelope and blank note card on a wooden table — exactly the candle-and-letter setup described for this grief-remembrance ritual.

Photo shows sliced dark offal pieces in a rich brown sauce over white mash/grains, with a whole onion and rosemary visible beside — a flux-schnell generated image that closely matches the liver and onions finished dish.

Photo shows Bananagrams letter tiles arranged to spell 'I CANT BREATHE' on a Bananagrams pouch — breath is the subject but the negative phrase and game-tile format is a mismatch for a calming breath-regulation practice.
Photo shows a macramé hammock suspended in a room — macramé knotwork is the right craft class but this is a large hanging hammock, not a knotted plant-holder basket for a pot.
Photo shows a knotted macramé bag/purse hanging under a table alongside other craft materials — macramé knotwork is the right class but this is a bag, not a flat-knotted table runner.

Photo shows a macramé wall hanging with long draping knotted cords above a bed headboard — macramé wall hanging is the right class but this is a cascading waterfall/curtain style rather than the specific semicircular sunrise fan design described.

Photo shows a blurred mother holding a newborn baby with a nursery mobile in the foreground — an evocative new-mother scene that is adjacent to matrescence but does not name or represent the psychological transformation itself.

Photo shows a woman dressed as a judge with a grey wig and scales of justice behind her, representing judgment/being judged — thematically adjacent to the affirmation's subject of having one's spiritual practice judged, but it depicts legal judgment not spiritual judgment.

Photo shows a neon sign reading 'TIME IS PRECIOUS' on a building exterior — picks up the time theme of the affirmation but is a decorative sign, not a visual representation of time being 'enough' or the affirmation practice itself.
Photo shows a pile of brown and orange needle-felted wool balls, not a needle-felted bee — completely different felted subject with no bee visible.

Photo shows a needle-felted white figure hanging as a Christmas tree ornament — it is a needle-felted hanging ornament, the right class, but the figure appears to be a snowman or elf rather than a robin-coloured bird.
Photo shows a pile of brown and orange needle-felted wool balls, not a needle-felted hedgehog — completely different felted subject with no hedgehog visible.
Photo shows a needle-felted grey rabbit with upright ears surrounded by colourful pom-poms, directly matching the tutorial's subject of a needle-felted sitting rabbit in grey merino.
Photo shows real live sheep and lambs grazing in a field, not the needle-felted miniature sheep flock that is the tutorial's subject.

Photo shows needle-felted wool spheres, which are simple 3D felted forms related to the armature-free sculpture technique, but they are basic balls rather than the finished animal or abstract sculptural forms the tutorial covers.

Photo shows a person's arm draped in flowing sheer white organza fabric — shows the organza material used in nuno felting but not the felting process or the characteristic textured, pleated nuno-felted cloth.

Photo shows candles sitting on small wooden dishes on a table — shows candles on a tray-like surface which is the use case for an oak candle tray, but the wooden tray itself is not an identifiable oak piece with chamfered edges.
Photo shows One Piece manga volumes (vol. 31) — books, not clothing or the act of wearing a fashion piece someone has deemed too young.

Photo shows a lit candle, dried herbs, and a piece of paper with text on a wooden bedside surface — a contemplative prayer/ritual still life that evokes the ritual setting, but no person is shown speaking a sentence of prayer.
Photo shows the word 'ONE' painted in large white letters on a blue brick wall — textually connects to 'one small thing' but is street art typography, not an image of doing a small manageable task.

Photo shows vibrantly dyed tie-dye fabric in rainbow colours — shows dyed textile which is the right class of output, but tie-dye is a resist-dyeing technique distinct from overdyeing, and no dye bath or fibre/yarn is visible.
Photo shows a pile of white wheat flour with a wheat stalk and a wooden spoon — a key ingredient, not the finished Pain rustique loaf.

Photo shows a sliced rustic white Italian-style loaf with thick crust, which is the right class of bread for pane pugliese, but the crumb appears tighter and more even than the open, moist crumb characteristic of this Apulian loaf.
Photo shows chocolate bars or bark coated with chopped pistachios and walnuts on a plate — chocolate nut confectionery, not peanut butter brownies with a peanut butter swirl.
Photo shows flour pouring from an overturned glass jar onto a wooden surface — an ingredient shot of flour, not the finished Yorkshire pikelets.

Photo shows multiple spice jars with metal lids arranged on rustic wooden shelving — shows the use case of a spice rack holding jars, but the rack is not identifiably pine wood and no construction detail is visible.
Photo shows three brown eggs on a floured surface — eggs are a key ingredient for pizzelle but this is an ingredient shot, not the finished thin crisp Italian waffle biscuits.
Photo shows a pan-fried pork chop topped with diced caramelised apple and onion with broccolini on a white plate — unambiguously matches the tutorial's pork chops with cider and apples dish.

Photo shows a plate with what appears to be a ground-meat patty or meatball-type item, sweet potato mash, and green beans — a different dish entirely, with no pork chop or mustard cream sauce visible.
Photo shows raw pork shoulder and belly cuts laid out on a wooden board — uncooked raw meat, not the finished hot-water-crust pork pie.

Photo shows cooked shrimp/prawns being drained from a pot into a colander — shows the key ingredient being cooked and handled, but not the finished potted shrimp packed into ramekins and sealed with spiced clarified butter.
Photo shows a tray of whole cooked prawns with heads on — shows the key ingredient (cooked prawns) but not the finished prawn cocktail presentation with Marie Rose sauce, shredded lettuce, and lemon.
Photo shows a decorative ceramic tea cup placed on a plain wooden disc — a tea cup on an undecorated wooden surface, with no pyrography burn marks, leaf design, or fire-work visible.
Photo shows a person studying financial or stock-market line charts on paper — a completely different type of chart from a weaving sett chart, different domain entirely.

Photo shows a neat white floating shelf with books, small potted plants, and a figurine arranged on it — directly and unambiguously depicts a styled shelf, which is the subject of the rearrange-one-shelf activity.
Photo shows colourful needle-felted wool balls — dryer balls or decorative felted spheres, not a resist-felted bowl shape.

Photo shows a floor loom (shaft loom) with white warp threads and heddles — weaving equipment in the right domain, but this is a multi-shaft floor loom, not the rigid heddle loom used in the tutorial.

Photo shows a person hammering a modern plastic/metal tent peg into the ground with a rubber mallet — shows the use case of tent pegs being driven in, but the peg is a manufactured metal one, not a hand-riven oak wooden peg.

Photo shows a sliced dense dark rye loaf with close-grained crumb on a wooden board — the characteristic appearance of Roggenbrot, matching the tutorial's description of a dense, close-crumbed German rye bread.
Photo shows devilled eggs on a tray — a completely different food item from Scandinavian rosettes, which are thin crisp fried batter cookies.

Photo shows a generous slice of a pastry-lidded pie with chunky filling on a plate with chips and greens — right class of dish (meat pie with pastry crust), but the filling looks like chicken or pork rather than salmon, and no dill is evident.
Photo shows meatballs in an orange sauce with polenta or mashed potato — a different dish entirely from sausage and mash with caramelised onions.
Photo shows two grilled bratwurst-style sausages on a plate with mustard — plain grilled sausages, not a sausage roll (no puff pastry encasing the sausagemeat).
Photo shows a pile of whole raw langoustines (Norway lobsters) at a market — the correct shellfish ingredient for scampi, but not the finished breaded and deep-fried dish.

Photo shows hands pressing and stretching flat bread dough on a floured surface — shows the technique stage of forming a flatbread, which is adjacent to schiacciata, but no grapes are pressed into it and the characteristic topping is absent.

Photo shows a bowl of clear broth soup with chunks of meat and root vegetables — shows the right class of dish (lamb and vegetable broth), but courgette and black beans are present instead of the pearl barley, swede, and leek of Scotch broth.
Photo shows raw red mince meat in a glass bowl — an uncooked ingredient, not the finished Shepherd's Pie with lamb filling under a mashed-potato crust.
Photo shows sliced leeks on a wooden cutting board with a knife — an ingredient being prepped, not the finished smoked haddock and leek pie.
Photo shows mixing bowls with dry baking ingredients and measuring cups of liquid — a baking ingredient prep shot, not the finished griddle-cooked soda farls.
Photo shows a sliced banana loaf on a board alongside whole and sliced bananas — directly and unambiguously shows banana bread, which is the tutorial subject.

Photo shows a bowl of waffle batter in the foreground with waffles and blueberries visible in the background — waffles are present and identifiable but the batter bowl dominates rather than the finished waffles; the specific sourdough character cannot be seen.
Photo shows a close-up portrait of a grey-blue faced sheep (which may be a BFL breed) — shows the animal that provides the fleece, but not the spinning process, drafting, or finished BFL yarn.

Photo shows hands drafting white wool fibre into a thin singles thread at a spinning wheel — clearly shows the spinning technique and wool fibre being worked, directly matching the tutorial's subject.

Photo shows an industrial silk-processing facility with large hanks of yellow/gold silk fibre hanging to dry and reeling equipment — shows silk fibre at scale, the right material class, but not the specific Mawata silk hankie product or the act of drafting from a hankie on a spindle.

Photo shows a restaurant-plated dish with a golden polenta/cornmeal round topped with mushroom, tomatoes, and kale — a polenta-based dish in the right class, but plated as a formal restaurant dish rather than the soft spoonable baked cornmeal pudding that is spoonbread.
Photo shows raw beef fillet steaks on a board next to a dish of sliced raw potatoes — raw meat and potato ingredients, not the finished steak and ale pie with braised chuck under a pastry lid.
Photo shows sliced seared steak cuts plated with greens and jus — no pastry casing or pie form, so it does not match Steak and Kidney Pie.
Same image as entry 100 — sliced steak on a plate with no suet crust or pudding form, so it does not match Steak and Kidney Pudding.
Same image again — sliced seared steak with no pie, pastry lid, or mushrooms visible, so it does not match Steak and Mushroom Pie.
Photo shows cut-out sugar cookies decorated with coloured royal icing and sprinkles on a cooling rack, which is exactly the finished subject of this tutorial.
Photo shows soft round buns with a crumbly, sugar-dusted cookie crust on a wooden rack — the characteristic appearance of Taiwanese pineapple buns (bolo bao).
Close-up of a woven textile showing a sharp diagonal colour boundary between red-orange and grey areas, which is precisely the characteristic output of tapestry colour blocking.
Photo shows a woman tapping/touching her collarbone area — shows the tapping technique being performed but does not distinguish this as a mum-rage practice specifically.
Photo shows a woman with both hands placed on her upper chest/collarbone in a tapping gesture — right class of tapping imagery but not specific to resentment in a marriage.
Photo shows a woman tapping near her collarbone area from behind — shows the tapping technique but carries no specific signal for the ageing body subject.
Photo shows a woman with fingers touching her collarbone/upper chest — shows tapping practice but is generic to all tapping tutorials, not specific to releasing a stuck event.
Photo shows a woman's hand resting on her collarbone/upper chest — shows tapping practice but carries no specific visual signal for the 'no' or boundary-setting subject.
Photo shows a woman's hand resting on her upper chest — shows tapping technique but is generic and does not specifically evoke parent loss or grief.
Photo shows a woman with a hand placed on her upper chest/collarbone — shows tapping practice but does not convey depression specifically over any other tapping tutorial.
Photo shows a baker mixing flour and eggs with a bowl of fresh strawberries nearby — the ingredients are recognisably for a strawberry tart but the finished tarte is not shown.

Photo shows crumpled notebook paper with a sticky note saying 'TAKE A BREAK!!' — conveys cognitive overwhelm and stress which is adjacent to the mental load concept but is generic.
Photo shows a letter board with 'WHAT IN THE ACTUAL HELL?' on a yellow background — captures midlife exasperation and questioning but is a generic exclamation rather than a belief-examination prompt.
Photo shows a weathered red 'SLOW' road sign overgrown in tall grass — loosely evokes the slow-road metaphor in the title but is a road sign rather than a person walking calmly.
Photo shows a couple at a café table smiling and embracing — right class of couple togetherness but no money, finance, or Sunday-date-specific element is visible.

Photo shows a styled slow-morning scene with a candle, herbs, paper, and a small bowl on a wooden side table — evokes the right class (slow morning ritual) without being specifically identifiable as 'The Sunday Slow Morning'.
Photo shows dark brown flour/meal with baking powder and buttermilk measuring cups — looks like treacle soda bread prep ingredients but no finished loaf is shown.

Photo shows a two-layer cake with caramel drip and fresh mixed berries on top — it is a layer cake but has no visible chocolate layers or chocolate frosting, so it does not match Triple Chocolate Layer Cake.

Photo shows a basket full of raw chestnut mushrooms — this is a single ingredient and there is no pastry, sausage roll form, or any indication of the finished Vegetarian Sausage Roll.
Photo shows red lentils, onions, turmeric, and garlic — plausible ingredients for a vegetarian shepherd's pie filling but no finished dish is shown.
Photo shows three dark seeded/whole-grain rye bread loaves with a wheat stalk — Vollkornbrot is a dense German whole-grain rye loaf and these loaves match its characteristic appearance exactly.
Photo shows a 'LOVE TO LEARN' sign on a wall near a pedestrian — this is unrelated to the tutorial 'We Can Learn to Talk Again', which is about communication in a partnership.

Photo shows a decorated celebration cake with white frosting, chocolate drip, and fresh fruit — it is a celebratory cake but not a traditional dark wedding fruit cake with dried fruits and royal icing.

Photo shows a sliced white sandwich loaf on a board — plain untoasted bread with no cheese sauce, so it does not represent the finished Welsh Rarebit.
Photo shows a close-up of colourful felted roses — wet felted decorative objects but not a bag with handles, which is the specific item for this tutorial.

Photo shows a handwritten letter on aged paper — completely unrelated to wet felted slippers.

Same image as entry 135 — colourful small felted balls, which shows wet felting output but not the specific technique of incorporating plant fibres into a merino base.

Photo shows several decorative glass bottles with stoppers — the bottle and stopper context is relevant but no hand-carved whittled wooden stopper is visible as the primary subject.
Photo shows a smiling baby in a medical cranial helmet — the baby is visible but the tutorial is a journal prompt about the mother's pre-baby identity, making this image misaligned.

Photo shows bronze sculpture figures in a public square fountain — urban street art with no connection to a willow bird feeder or basketry.
Photo shows a fan of brightly coloured woven reed/straw placemats — the finished product matches the tutorial subject exactly.
